docs.title: sim-rating
docs.text:
sim-rating is a small PHP library that turns five star rating counts into a clean average, a distribution, and a ready to display widget. It works with any PHP project, including Laravel, Symfony, CodeIgniter, and plain PHP.

You give it how many people left one, two, three, four, and five stars. It gives you back the maths and the markup, so you do not have to build a rating display from scratch every time.

docs.title: What you get
docs.text:
• A weighted average, a total count, and a percentage distribution.
  • Four output formats: HTML stars, HTML bars, a standalone SVG, and JSON.
  • A namespaced set of CSS classes so you can style everything from your own stylesheet.
  • Safe output. Every value that reaches the page is checked and escaped first.
  • Full test coverage, static analysis, and a code style check.

docs.title: A quick look
docs.text:
use Emleons\SimRating\Rating;

$rating = new Rating([
    'one_star'   => 10,
    'two_star'   => 20,
    'three_star' => 30,
    'four_star'  => 40,
    'five_star'  => 50,
]);

echo $rating->render();          // HTML stars
echo $rating->getAverage();      // 3.67
echo $rating->getTotal();        // 150

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text: sim-rating needs PHP 8.3 or newer. It has no required runtime dependencies, so installing it adds nothing else to your project.

docs.title: Where to go next
docs.text:
• New here? Start with Installation, then the Quickstart.
  • Want to change how it looks? Read Styling.
  • Need the full list of settings? See the Options reference.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: This page summarises recent changes. The complete history lives in CHANGELOG.md in the repository root, kept in the Keep a Changelog format with Semantic Versioning.

docs.title: Unreleased
docs.text:
• Namespaced BEM classes on every element (em-sim-rating family), with the legacy classes kept as secondary output for compatibility.
  • New instance_id option for stable per widget targeting.
  • New inline_styles option to omit the default style block when you ship dist/sim-rating.css yourself.
  • New canonical stylesheet at dist/sim-rating.css, driven by theme variables.
  • Default bar CSS is now scoped per instance, so multiple widgets on one page stay independent.

docs.title: Version 2.2.0
docs.text:
A production hardening release. Public constructors, render(), and getters stayed compatible.

  • Strict typing across all of src, plus StarKey and DisplayType enums and a central Escaper for output safety.
  • Per render option overrides that leave the instance unchanged.
  • New strict and empty_color options, and accessible markup with roles and labels.
  • Tooling: Pint, PHPStan at level 8, and one command quality gate.
  • Fixed: colour and size injection closed, unique SVG ids per instance, and the SVG renderer now returns real SVG instead of JSON.

docs.title: Version 2.1.2
docs.text: • Fixed an undefined array key warning for the show_summary option.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: Thanks for your interest in sim-rating. This page covers the local setup and the quality bar. The full text also lives in CONTRIBUTING.md in the repository root.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
You need PHP 8.3 or newer and Composer.

git clone git@github.com:emleonstz/sim-rating.git
cd sim-rating
composer install

docs.title: The quality gate
docs.text:
One command runs everything CI runs:

composer check

That is shorthand for three steps:

composer lint     # code style check, Pint in test mode
composer analyse  # static analysis, PHPStan at level 8
composer test     # test suite, PHPUnit

Run composer lint:fix to repair style automatically. Run composer test:coverage for a coverage report, which needs pcov or xdebug.

Every pull request must leave all three green.

docs.title: Code standards
docs.text:
• Start every PHP file with declare(strict_types=1);.
  • Type all parameters and return values. Annotate array shapes so PHPStan stays quiet.
  • Send every value that reaches markup through the Escaper helper.
  • Keep the public API stable where possible. If a change breaks callers, say so plainly in the pull request and add a changelog entry.
  • Add or update tests with each behaviour change. Security fixes need a regression test under tests/Security/.

docs.title: Commits and releases
docs.text:
Write clear conventional messages such as fix:, feat:, docs:, refactor:, or test:. To release, add a version section to CHANGELOG.md, then tag with git tag vX.Y.Z and push the tag.

By contributing you agree your work ships under the MIT License in the repository root.

docs.title: Security
docs.text: Rating widgets sit on public pages and often display data that came from visitors. sim-rating treats every value as untrusted until it has been checked. This page describes the model so you can review it with confidence.

docs.title: What is escaped
docs.text: All rendered output passes through the Escaper helper before it reaches the page. Colours, sizes, spacing values, labels, counts, percentages, ids, and text all go through validation or HTML escaping first. A hostile string such as a script tag in a colour option is neutralised or replaced with the safe default. It is never printed as given.

docs.title: What is validated
docs.text: Options with a fixed shape use allow lists. color and empty_color accept hex codes, rgb functions, and plain colour names. size and the bar dimensions accept numeric CSS lengths with safe units. The instance_id used for per widget styling is slugified for class use and escaped for attribute use. Anything that fails validation falls back to the default for that option.

docs.title: No raw CSS option
docs.text: The library offers no setting that prints caller supplied CSS verbatim. Allowing that would punch a hole straight through the escaping described above. Customise appearance through the documented classes, theme variables, and validated options instead. The Styling page shows the full set.

docs.title: Scripts without user data
docs.text: The optional interactive stars emit a sim-rating:change browser event so your JavaScript can react to clicks. That script block is fully static. It carries no user values inside it and reads state from data attributes at runtime. There is no eval and no string built from user input anywhere in the library.

docs.title: Instance isolation
docs.text: Each render gets its own identity. SVG gradient ids are unique per instance, and the default bar stylesheet is scoped to the instance id. One widget cannot restyle or relabel another on the same page.

docs.title: What stays your job
docs.text: The library does no storage and no network calls. It cannot know where your counts came from. Keep validating and authorising the data on your side, especially if counts can be submitted by visitors. Escape on output in the rest of your templates as well, and prefer {!! !!} or |raw only for the already safe render string.

docs.title: Reporting a problem
docs.text: If you find a bypass or a suspicious output, please report it privately by email to emleons23@gmail.com instead of opening a public issue. Include the version, a short reproduction, and the output you saw. Reports are acknowledged within 72 hours. Full details live in SECURITY.md in the repository root.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text: sim-rating needs PHP 8.3 or newer. It has no required runtime dependencies.

docs.title: Install with Composer
docs.text:
From your project root, run:

composer require emleons/sim-rating

Composer downloads the library and sets up autoloading. After that, the classes are ready to use.

docs.title: Check it works
docs.text:
Create a small PHP file to confirm everything is wired up:

<?php

require __DIR__ . '/vendor/autoload.php';

use Emleons\SimRating\Rating;

$rating = new Rating(['five_star' => 5]);

echo $rating->getAverage(); // 5

Run it with php yourfile.php. If you see 5, the install worked.

docs.title: Using it inside a framework
docs.text:
sim-rating is a normal PHP library, so it drops into any framework. A few notes:

  • Laravel: the package is autoloaded by Composer. In a Blade view you can build the object in your controller and pass it to the view, then print it with {!! $rating->render() !!}.
  • Symfony: create the object in your controller and pass it to Twig, then print with {{ rating.render()|raw }}.
  • CodeIgniter 4: create the object in your controller and pass the rendered string to your view.

If your project already uses Composer autoloading, there is nothing extra to configure.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: This documentation provides a comprehensive guide to implementing the rating widget, enabling you to achieve a functional integration quickly.

docs.title: The basic pattern
docs.text:
Every example follows the same two steps. First you create a Rating object with your counts. Then you print something from it.

use Emleons\SimRating\Rating;

$rating = new Rating([
    'one_star'   => 10,
    'two_star'   => 20,
    'three_star' => 30,
    'four_star'  => 40,
    'five_star'  => 50,
]);

Missing keys default to zero, so new Rating(['five_star' => 5]) is valid. If you want the library to insist on all five keys, pass 'strict' => true in the options. You can read more about that in the Options reference.

docs.title: Stars
docs.text:
Stars are the default output. This is the right choice for product pages, review summaries, and anywhere people expect the familiar row of stars.

echo $rating->render();

To hide the average or the total count:

echo $rating->render('html', [
    'show_average' => false,
    'show_total'   => true,
]);

To change the look:

echo $rating->render('html', [
    'color'       => '#e74c3c',
    'empty_color' => '#eee',
    'size'        => '1.5rem',
]);

docs.title: Bars
docs.text:
Bars show the full distribution, one row per star level. They suit analytics pages, admin screens, and detailed review sections.

echo $rating->render('html', ['type' => 'bars']);

Bar specific settings live alongside the normal ones:

echo $rating->render('html', [
    'type'                 => 'bars',
    'color'                => '#4a90e2',
    'bar_height'           => '25px',
    'bar_show_percentages' => true,
    'show_summary'         => true,
]);

docs.title: SVG
docs.text:
The SVG format returns a standalone picture with no extra markup around it. Use it in emails, PDFs, image pipelines, or anywhere you need one portable graphic.

echo $rating->render('svg');

docs.title: JSON
docs.text:
JSON returns the numbers without any markup. Use it when your frontend renders the widget itself, or when you are building an API response.

echo $rating->render('json');

The decoded shape looks like this:

{
    "average": 3.67,
    "total": 150,
    "distribution": {
        "one_star": 6.67,
        "two_star": 13.33,
        "three_star": 20.0,
        "four_star": 26.67,
        "five_star": 33.33
    }
}

docs.title: Reading the numbers directly
docs.text:
You can also skip rendering and use the maths in your own code:

$rating->getAverage();      // 3.67
$rating->getTotal();        // 150
$rating->getDistribution(); // array of five percentages
$rating->getRatings();      // the normalised counts

docs.title: What's next
docs.text:
• Display types explains each format in depth.
  • Styling shows how to match the widget to your site.
  • Options reference lists every setting.

docs.title: Display types
docs.text: sim-rating can present the same data in four ways. The numbers never change, only the presentation. This page helps you pick the right one.

docs.title: HTML stars
docs.text:
echo $rating->render('html');

This is the default. It prints a row of five stars with partial fill for fractional averages, plus the average value and total count beside them. Start here unless you have a reason to use something else.

Stars fit product cards, search results, review headers, and any place where space is tight and readers expect the classic pattern.

Two settings change the structure most often:

echo $rating->render('html', [
    'type'         => 'stars',
    'show_average' => true,
    'show_total'   => true,
]);

Set either one to false to hide that part.

docs.title: HTML bars
docs.text:
echo $rating->render('html', ['type' => 'bars']);

Bars print five labelled rows, one per star level, with a track, a fill, and the percentage. A summary line with the average and total can appear below. Bars answer the question "how are the votes spread", where stars only answer "what is the score".

Bars fit review sections, dashboards, and admin pages. They need more width than stars, roughly a card or a column, to read well.

The bar specific options are listed in full in the Options reference. The most used ones:

echo $rating->render('html', [
    'type'                   => 'bars',
    'bar_height'             => '20px',
    'bar_spacing'            => '8px',
    'bar_border_radius'      => '4px',
    'bar_show_counts'        => true,
    'bar_show_percentages'   => true,
    'bar_percentage_precision' => 1,
]);

docs.title: SVG
docs.text:
echo $rating->render('svg');

SVG returns one standalone svg element with the stars drawn as shapes. It needs no fonts, no icon set, and no stylesheet. The colour and size options still apply.

Use SVG for HTML emails, PDF invoices, social preview images, feeds, and any context where linked CSS may not load. If you need the numbers too, pair it with a json call and place the text yourself.

docs.title: JSON
docs.text:
echo $rating->render('json');

JSON returns average, total, and distribution as a JSON string. It is meant for machines, not readers. Typical uses are JavaScript frontends that draw their own widget, mobile apps fetching scores over HTTP, and cached API responses.

$data = json_decode($rating->render('json'), true);

echo $data['average']; // 3.67
echo $data['total'];   // 150

docs.title: Type safe selection
docs.text:
If you prefer objects over strings, the DisplayType enum offers the same three formats with IDE support:

use Emleons\SimRating\Enum\DisplayType;

echo $rating->render(DisplayType::Html);
echo $rating->render(DisplayType::Svg);
echo $rating->render(DisplayType::Json);

An unknown string throws an InvalidArgumentException with the value in the message, so typos fail loudly instead of rendering the wrong thing.

docs.title: Per render overrides
docs.text:
The second argument to render() adjusts options for that call only. The object itself is left unchanged, so later renders use the original settings.

echo $rating->render('html', ['color' => '#e74c3c']); // red, this once
echo $rating->render(); // back to the instance colour

docs.title: Options reference
docs.text:
Every setting below can be passed to the constructor or changed later with setOptions(). The render() method also accepts overrides for a single call without changing the object.

use Emleons\SimRating\Rating;

$rating = new Rating($counts, [
    'color' => '#e74c3c',
    'size'  => '1.5rem',
]);

$rating->setOptions(['show_total' => false]);

echo $rating->render('html', ['color' => '#2ecc71']); // this call only

docs.title: type
docs.text:
Which layout the HTML renderer prints. Allowed values are stars and bars. Default is stars.

['type' => 'bars']

docs.title: color
docs.text:
The fill colour for stars and bars. Accepts hex, rgb, and plain colour names. Anything outside the allow list falls back to the default instead of being printed. Default is #ffc107.

['color' => '#e74c3c']

docs.title: empty_color
docs.text:
The colour of the unfilled part of a star. Validated the same way as color. Default is #ddd.

['empty_color' => '#eee']

docs.title: size
docs.text:
The star size, as a CSS length such as 1em, 24px, or 1.5rem. Values outside the allow list fall back to the default. Default is 1em.

['size' => '1.5rem']

docs.title: show_average
docs.text: Show the numeric average beside the stars. Default is true.

docs.title: show_total
docs.text: Show the total vote count beside the stars. Default is true.

docs.title: show_summary
docs.text:
Show the summary line under the bars layout. Default is true.

['show_average' => false, 'show_total' => true, 'show_summary' => true]

docs.title: interactive
docs.text: Render clickable stars that emit a sim-rating:change browser event with the chosen value. The script is static and reads from data attributes, so no user input ever lands inside JavaScript. Default is false.

docs.title: readonly
docs.text: Marks the widget as readonly for assistive tech. Default is true.

docs.title: instance_id
docs.text: A stable identity for one widget placement, for example product-42. It is printed as a data-sim-rating-id attribute and a scope class, and unsafe characters are stripped. When left as null, a unique id is generated per render. Default is null.

docs.title: inline_styles
docs.text: When true, the bars layout prints a small scoped style block with its defaults. Set to false when you include dist/sim-rating.css yourself. Default is true.

docs.title: strict
docs.text:
When true, constructing or updating the object throws unless all five rating keys are present. When false, missing keys are treated as zero. Default is false.

new Rating($data, ['strict' => true]);

docs.title: Bar layout
docs.text: These only affect type => bars.

docs.title: bar_height
docs.text: Thickness of each bar track. Default is 20px.

docs.title: bar_spacing
docs.text: Vertical space between bar rows. Default is 8px.

docs.title: bar_border_radius
docs.text: Corner rounding of tracks and fills. Default is 4px.

docs.title: bar_show_counts
docs.text: Show the raw vote count on each row. Default is true.

docs.title: bar_show_percentages
docs.text: Show the percentage on each row. Default is true.

docs.title: bar_percentage_precision
docs.text: How many decimals the percentages print with. Default is 1.

docs.title: bar_percentage_suffix
docs.text: Text printed right after each percentage value. Default is %. Set to an empty string to drop it.

docs.title: bar_animate
docs.text:
Animate the fill width when the page loads. Default is true.

[
    'type'                     => 'bars',
    'bar_height'               => '25px',
    'bar_spacing'              => '8px',
    'bar_border_radius'        => '4px',
    'bar_show_counts'          => true,
    'bar_show_percentages'     => true,
    'bar_percentage_precision' => 1,
    'bar_percentage_suffix'    => '%',
    'bar_animate'              => true,
]

docs.title: Styling
docs.text: The widget ships with sensible default looks, but real projects need their own identity. sim-rating gives you three clean ways to customise appearance, all from your own stylesheet. There is deliberately no option that accepts raw CSS text, and the Security page explains why.

docs.title: The class system
docs.text:
Every rendered element carries two classes. The first is the namespaced BEM class. That is the one to target. The second is the legacy class, kept so older stylesheets keep working.

  • Root: em-sim-rating (legacy: sim-rating)
  • Stars wrapper: em-sim-rating__stars
  • Each star: em-sim-rating__star (legacy: sim-rating-star)
  • Average value: em-sim-rating__average (legacy: sim-rating-average)
  • Total count: em-sim-rating__total (legacy: sim-rating-total)
  • Bars root: em-sim-rating__bars (legacy: sim-rating-bars-container)
  • One bar row: em-sim-rating__bar (legacy: sim-rating-bar)
  • Bar label: em-sim-rating__bar-label (legacy: sim-rating-bar-label)
  • Bar track: em-sim-rating__bar-track (legacy: sim-rating-bar-bg)
  • Bar fill: em-sim-rating__bar-fill (legacy: sim-rating-bar-fill)
  • Bar percentage: em-sim-rating__bar-percent (legacy: sim-rating-bar-percent)
  • Summary line: em-sim-rating__summary (legacy: sim-rating-summary)
  • SVG root: em-sim-rating__svg (legacy: sim-rating-svg)

A simple override looks like this:

.em-sim-rating__average {
    font-weight: 700;
}

.em-sim-rating__bar-fill {
    border-radius: 999px;
}

The legacy classes are deprecated and will be removed in a future major release, so write all new CSS against the em-sim-rating names.

docs.title: The published stylesheet
docs.text:
The file dist/sim-rating.css holds the canonical styles. Include it once in your page, then render with inline styles switched off to avoid a repeated style block per widget:

echo $rating->render('html', ['inline_styles' => false]);

<link rel="stylesheet" href="/vendor/emleons/sim-rating/dist/sim-rating.css">

Adjust the path to match where Composer installed the package in your project, or copy the file into your own assets folder.

docs.title: Theme variables
docs.text:
The published stylesheet is driven by custom properties. Override any of them on the widget root to retheme without writing new rules:

.em-sim-rating {
    --em-sim-rating-color: #ffc107;
    --em-sim-rating-empty-color: #ddd;
    --em-sim-rating-size: 1em;
    --em-sim-rating-gap: 2px;
    --em-sim-rating-font: system stack;
    --em-sim-rating-bar-height: 20px;
    --em-sim-rating-bar-spacing: 8px;
    --em-sim-rating-bar-radius: 4px;
    --em-sim-rating-bar-track: #f5f5f5;
}

The quick PHP side equivalents are the color, empty_color, size, bar_height, bar_spacing, and bar_border_radius options. Use the options for one widget and the variables for a whole site.

docs.title: Targeting one widget
docs.text:
Pass instance_id to give a widget a stable identity. It appears as a data-sim-rating-id attribute and as a scope class, so you can style one placement without touching the others:

echo $rating->render('html', ['instance_id' => 'product-42']);

.em-sim-rating[data-sim-rating-id="product-42"] {
    --em-sim-rating-color: #e74c3c;
}

Without an explicit id, each render generates a unique one, and the default inline bar CSS is scoped to it. Multiple widgets on one page never share styles by accident.

docs.title: Quick recipes
docs.text:
Bigger stars with a warm colour:

echo $rating->render('html', [
    'color' => '#f39c12',
    'size'  => '1.5rem',
]);

Slim bars with counts hidden:

echo $rating->render('html', [
    'type'            => 'bars',
    'bar_height'      => '10px',
    'bar_show_counts' => false,
]);

Dark track for a dark theme, from your stylesheet:

.dark-theme .em-sim-rating {
    --em-sim-rating-bar-track: #333;
    --em-sim-rating-empty-color: #555;
}
